title: Stable placement in counting sort using prefix sums
summary: Accumulate frequencies into prefix sums to find destination indices. Scan the input backward, filling res and decrementing the counts, then copy res over nums.
context: The original array is nums = [1, 0, 1, 2, 0, 4, 0, 2, 2, 4] (indices 0 through 9). Values range from 0 through 4, with frequencies counter = [3, 2, 3, 0, 2].

Accumulating the counts in counter gives the initial prefix = [3, 5, 8, 8, 10]. Initially prefix[num] counts elements less than or equal to num. For a value num that occurs, prefix[num] - 1 gives the last index it will occupy in res. The figure calls these sums prefix; the code stores them in counter, overwriting its frequencies.

The result array res has ten slots. Blank cells mean nothing has been placed yet and differ from cells that already contain the value 0. The code initializes res with zeros, while the drawing leaves unwritten cells blank.
description: Scan nums from right to left. Write the current value num to res[prefix[num] − 1], then decrease prefix[num] by 1. If another equal value remains, the new prefix[num] − 1 gives its destination. The entries in prefix change during placement and no longer hold the original prefix sums.

Scanning backward while filling each value’s result positions from right to left preserves stability. Equal elements farther right in the input take the farther-right positions first, leaving earlier elements to their left. The first four writes shown use original indices 9, 8, 7, and 6. The next six are skipped on screen before the completed result array res is shown and copied over nums.

frames.title: Count frequencies
frames.explanation: Scan nums to count the occurrences of 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, producing the length-5 array counter = [3, 2, 3, 0, 2]. Prefix sums have not been calculated and nothing has been written to the result.
frames.announcement: Frequencies: 0 occurs 3 times, 1 occurs 2 times, 2 occurs 3 times, 3 occurs 0 times, and 4 occurs 2 times.

state_tables.caption: Counting sort, step 1: frequencies in counter

frames.title: Accumulate the frequencies and prepare the result array
frames.explanation: Accumulate counter to obtain prefix = [3, 5, 8, 8, 10], and prepare ten blank slots in res. Using prefix[num] - 1, the last destination for 0 is 3 - 1 = 2, for 2 it is 8 - 1 = 7, and for 4 it is 10 - 1 = 9. Value 3 is absent and will never be written.
frames.key_state: Prefix sums are prefix = [3, 5, 8, 8, 10]. No elements have been placed in res yet.
frames.announcement: Accumulate frequencies into prefix sums in prefix to find the last available index in res for each value that occurs.

frames.title: Write the final 4 at index 9
frames.explanation: The num marker points to the rightmost input index 9, holding 4. Before this write, prefix[4] = 10, giving destination 10 - 1 = 9. Write 4 to res[9], then decrement prefix[4] by 1 to 9. The figure shows prefix after the decrement. Only original index 9 has been processed; the other nine slots remain empty.
frames.key_state: From original index 9, 4 has been written to res[9] = 4, and prefix[4] decreased to 9. The other nine slots remain empty.
frames.announcement: Read 4 from original index 9 in the right-to-left scan, write it at result index 9, and decrease prefix[4] by 1.

frames.title: Write 2 from original index 8 at index 7
frames.explanation: The num marker moves left to input index 8, holding 2. Before this write, prefix[2] = 8, giving destination 8 - 1 = 7. Write 2 to res[7], then decrement prefix[2] by 1 to 7. The figure shows prefix after the decrement. Original indices 9 down to 8 have been processed.
frames.key_state: From original index 8, 2 has been written to res[7] = 2, and prefix[2] decreased to 7. Original indices 9 down to 8 have been processed.
frames.announcement: Read 2 from original index 8 in the right-to-left scan, write it at result index 7, and decrease prefix[2] by 1.

frames.title: Write 2 from original index 7 at index 6
frames.explanation: The num marker moves left to input index 7, holding 2. This is the second 2 encountered from the right. The preceding write decremented prefix[2] to 7. Before this write, prefix[2] = 7, giving destination 7 - 1 = 6. Write 2 to res[6] to the left of the previous 2, preserving their original order, then decrement prefix[2] by 1 to 6. The figure shows prefix after the decrement. Original indices 9 down to 7 have been processed.
frames.key_state: From original index 7, 2 has been written to res[6] = 2, and prefix[2] decreased to 6. Original indices 9 down to 7 have been processed.
frames.announcement: Read 2 from original index 7 in the right-to-left scan, write it at result index 6, and decrease prefix[2] by 1.

frames.title: Write 0 from original index 6 at index 2
frames.explanation: The num marker moves left to input index 6, holding 0. Before this write, prefix[0] = 3, giving destination 3 - 1 = 2. Write 0 to res[2], then decrement prefix[0] by 1 to 2. The figure shows prefix after the decrement. Original indices 9 down to 6 have been processed; res[2] holds a written 0, while “Not yet written” means no element has been placed.
frames.key_state: From original index 6, 0 has been written to res[2] = 0, and prefix[0] decreased to 2. Original indices 9 down to 6 have been processed.
frames.announcement: Read 0 from original index 6 in the right-to-left scan, write it at result index 2, and decrease prefix[0] by 1.

frames.title: Finish the other six writes
frames.explanation: Continue backward through original indices 5 down to 0. Their six values, 4, 0, 2, 1, 0, 1, go to indices 8, 1, 5, 4, 0, 3 of res respectively. The figure skips these six intermediate writes. At the end of the scan res holds the entire sorted sequence. The original array nums above it has not yet been overwritten.
frames.key_state: Result array res contains the full ascending sequence, while nums still has its original order.
frames.announcement: The remaining six writes in reverse input order are complete. The entire result array res is sorted.

state_tables.caption: Counting sort, step 7: prefix after decrementing

frames.title: Copy the result back to nums
frames.explanation: Copy all ten elements from sorted res back into nums at their corresponding indices. The upper array nums becomes [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4], completing counting sort. The final prefix = [0, 3, 5, 8, 8]. For the values that occur, 0, 1, 2, and 4, these entries give their first indices in res: 0, 3, 5, and 8. Value 3 does not occur, so prefix[3] = 8 does not point to a 3; it matches the first index of 4. Final prefix[num] counts the input elements strictly less than num. For example, 8 elements are less than 3, giving 8 even though 3 is absent.
frames.key_state: Result array res has been copied over nums. Counting sort is complete.
frames.announcement: Overwrite nums with sorted res to complete counting sort.
